1.  **Buffer Not Full:** If the number of fragments currently in the k-buffer is less than $k$, insert the new fragment into the correct position to maintain ascending order by comparing it with existing fragments [S1].

The claim states that if the number of fragments in the k-buffer is less than k, the new fragment is inserted into the correct position to maintain ascending order by comparing it with existing fragments. Source [S1] explicitly confirms this in the 'Fragment Processing (Sorted k-buffer)' section (Step 1) and in the detailed description under Section II ('When the number of fragments in k-buffer is smaller than k, the new fragment compares with the fragments already in the buffer and is inserted into the right position'). The source also notes that the optimization keeps the k-buffer sorted in ascending order.
supported

Optimized HAVS (Sorted k-buffer) is an optimization of the Hardware Assisted Visibility Sorting (HAVS) algorithm that maintains the k-buffer in ascending order of fragment distance to reduce the computational cost of fragment-level visibility sorting [S1].

The claim states that Optimized HAVS maintains the k-buffer in ascending order of fragment distance to reduce computational cost. Source [S1] explicitly states that the optimization involves 'keeping a sorted list' (specifically the k-buffer) to 'decrease the comparing time' (computational cost). The notes and passages confirm that this sorted approach reduces comparisons from 2k-1 to k per step, thereby supporting the claim that it reduces computational cost.
supported
